title: Air India Unveils India-Inspired Amenity Kits and Loungewear for Long-Haul Premium Passengers
excerpt: Gond art, Navratna colours, a wooden Marma massager and Kullu-inspired loungewear arrive on flights over eight hours from October 2026
body:
• Air India is rolling out new amenity kits and loungewear for First and Business Class guests on international flights, created with Ayurvedic brand Forest Essentials.
  • Passengers get the new experience from October 2026 on flights exceeding eight hours and on overnight flights of over six hours.
  • First Class kits carry collectible Gond art by Dwarka Paraste; Business Class kits use the nine colours of the Navratna in a Jharoka-shaped bag.
  • Both premium cabins also receive a handcrafted wooden Ayurvedic Marma massager, which Air India describes as a first for an airline amenity kit, while Premium Economy gets a refreshed kit.

Air India has unveiled a new collection of premium guest amenities and loungewear for its First and Business Class passengers on international flights, drawing the designs from Indian art, textiles and wellness traditions rather than from a generic luxury template. The collection, created in collaboration with luxury Ayurvedic brand Forest Essentials, is part of the airline's ongoing transformation and will be rolled out from October 2026 across flights exceeding eight hours and on overnight flights of over six hours.

For diaspora travellers, the change is easy to identify. Long routes between India and North America, Europe and Australia cross the eight-hour threshold, so premium-cabin passengers on those services are the ones who will receive the new kits, massager and loungewear. Premium Economy gets a refreshed, smaller kit. Fares, baggage and shorter services are unchanged.

First Class: Gond art as a collectible

First Class kits form what Air India calls The Art of Flight collection. Each kit features original Gond artwork created exclusively for the airline by artist Dwarka Paraste, with motifs intended to evoke nature, movement and discovery. Kits in Ivory Cream will be offered on flights departing India and Antique White kits on flights arriving in the country. The airline says the artwork and colour palette will be refreshed every six months, turning the kits into a collectible series rather than a single seasonal design.

https://x.com/airindia/status/2115032479782654239

"Premium Economy gets a refreshed, smaller kit."

Inside, Forest Essentials products are presented in a satin pouch: a Light Day Lotion with SPF 30, a Facial Tonic Mist, Lip Cream, Ultra-Rich Body Milk and intense perfume, alongside socks, an eye mask, ear plugs, a dental kit, a hair tie and a story card. Air India's own guest amenities page confirms the Paraste designs and the six-month refresh.

Business Class: the Navratna collection

Business Class guests will receive kits from the Navratna Collection, inspired by the Navratna, or nine gems of Indian tradition, and interpreted through nine distinctive colours. The kits come in Air India's signature Jharoka-shaped bag, crafted in premium PU leather and modelled on the jharokha architectural form. They are offered in Coral on flights departing India and Ruby on flights arriving in the country.

https://www.instagram.com/p/De_jdCJgQ38/

Business Class contents are narrower: Forest Essentials Lip Cream, Ultra-Rich Body Milk and intense perfume in a satin pouch, with socks, an eye mask, ear plugs, a dental kit, a hair tie and a story card. Direction of travel determines the colour, and repeat travellers can expect new colourways every six months.

A Marma massager and a Premium Economy refresh

Both First and Business Class guests will also receive a handcrafted Ayurvedic Marma massager made from 100 percent natural wood. Air India presents it as a first-of-its-kind inclusion in an airline amenity kit. It draws on the Ayurvedic practice of stimulating Marma points to promote relaxation and wellbeing during travel, and it comes with a dedicated story card.

Premium Economy's refreshed kit comes in a reusable Air India-branded bag, with hand cream and lip balm by The Indian Apothecary, socks, an eye mask and a story card — a simpler offer that extends the redesign beyond the front cabin.

Loungewear inspired by the Kullu shawl

The loungewear for First and Business Class is inspired by Himachal Pradesh's Kullu shawl-weaving tradition. Its geometric motifs appear on the placket and hem of a Henley-style top and on the drawstring and side placket of the bottoms, in a gender-neutral design in soft fabric. The set comes in four sizes, including a newly introduced XXL, in a bespoke carry bag with a story card. Carpet slippers change from grey to beige to match the palette.

What happens next

The rollout begins in October 2026 on eligible long-haul and overnight services, with designs refreshing every six months, so a winter kit should differ from the following summer's. Whether passengers keep them will depend on quality, but the direction is clear: Air India is trying to make its premium cabin feel specifically Indian on its longest journeys.
